assumptions_resolved: A hosted runner holds no sole-orchestrator marker, so --reconcile-flow on a schedule would in fact report only. That is an environmental accident, not a guarantee, and the plan forbids relying on it. reportOnlyFlowIo removes the write capability before the reconciler sees the adapter, so the guarantee is structural: resolveMarker reads as gone and each of relinquishCapacity, resumeCapacity and persistReady throws if reached. A run that tried to write fails loudly.

The new command's exit codes do not touch --reconcile-flow's. That branch still returns 0 or 2 exactly as before; 3 exists only on the new --abandonment-audit branch, where it means the state could not be read. Both branches are exercised in the same test file so a change to either shows up against the other.

The workflow was given issues: read and pull-requests: read rather than no scopes at all, because the audit reads claims, work issues and pull requests through the GitHub API and would otherwise fail closed on every run. It was NOT given issues: write, so it cannot file the duplicate alarm issues an hourly monitor would otherwise produce -- the model workflow migration-ledger-drift.yml needs that scope for its throttled alarm and this one deliberately does not.

The workflow's own header comment names `push:`, `pull_request:` and `--reconcile-flow` in prose explaining why each is absent. The first policy test failed on exactly that, which is the right failure from a test scanning raw text: it was corrected to scan declaration lines and non-comment lines, and both scanners carry a positive control so a scanner that matched nothing cannot pass as a clean result.

No open non-draft pull request holds any file in allowed_paths. Pull requests 2823, 2821 and 2607 hold other workflow files; none holds this new workflow, either lane script, the reconcile test or the canonical guard test. The single-ready-PR collision rule is therefore satisfied rather than bypassed.
